<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I have all the information I need to create a comprehensive plan for the System Settings screen. Let me organize the settings into logical groups:

1. **AI / Anthropic** - API key (secret), model selection, max tokens, fast model, rate limits, pricing
2. **JIRA** - base URL, user, API token (secret), transitions, labels, defaults
3. **Git Platform** - platform selection (dropdown), username, password (secret), author name/email
4. **Platform-specific** - Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, GitLab, GitHub (conditional based on git.platform)
5. **Notifications** - Teams webhook, n8n webhook


6. **Security / API** - API key, webhook secrets for each platform, settings encryption key
7. **Agent Behavior** - max concurrent jobs, blocked paths, allowed commands, file/line change limits, loop iterations, timeout, build retries, self-review
8. **Schedulers** - quality-report, upgrade, code-graph schedulers
9. **Linter/SAST** - enabled flags for various tools like checkstyle, pmd, spotbugs, eslint
10. **Voyage AI** - API key, model, batch size
11. **Confluence** - base URL, user, API token
12. **PR Review** - skip authors, PR summary, sequence diagrams
13. **Code Metrics** - CC threshold, max iterations

The API structure is straightforward: I can fetch all stored overrides, get or update individual settings with metadata like whether they're secret, and delete settings to revert to defaults. The key insight is that the API only returns settings that have been explicitly set in the database, so the UI needs to handle loading defaults from properties and only displaying what's been overridden.

For the UI approach, I'm going with loading all overrides at once via `GET /settings`, then displaying all known settings grouped by category with indicators for which ones are using defaults. This lets me show the complete picture without making individual calls for each setting. I'll organize the page with collapsible sections for each category, inline editing with save/delete actions, and special handling for secret fields with password inputs and show/hide toggles. I need to add type definitions for the setting objects and requests, create the new settings page, and wire it into the routing and menu.</details></think>

  "plan": "# System Settings Screen\n\n## API Contract\n\n- &#96;GET /settings&#96; — returns all DB-stored overrides as &#96;SystemSetting[]&#96; (secrets masked as &#96;****&#96;)\n- &#96;PUT /settings/{key}&#96; — body: &#96;{ value, isSecret, description }&#96;\n- &#96;DELETE /settings/{key}&#96; — reverts key to env-var/properties default\n\nThe frontend defines the full catalog of known keys (groups + metadata) statically — since &#96;GET /settings&#96; only returns keys that have been overridden, not all possible keys.\n\n## Files to Change\n\n- [&#96;src/types/api.ts&#96;](src/types/api.ts) — add &#96;SystemSetting&#96; and &#96;UpsertSettingRequest&#96; types\n- [&#96;src/main.tsx&#96;](src/main.tsx) — import and register &#96;systemSettingsRoute&#96; at &#96;/settings/system&#96;\n- [&#96;src/config/applicationMenu.tsx&#96;](src/config/applicationMenu.tsx) — add \"System\" child item under the Settings section\n- **New file** &#96;src/pages/SystemSettings.tsx&#96; — the full page component\n\n## Page Architecture\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    SystemSettings[\"SystemSettings page\"]\n    Query[\"useQuery GET /settings\\n(all overrides)\"]\n    Groups[\"SETTING_GROUPS\\n(static catalog)\"]\n    Accordion[\"Accordion sections\\nper category\"]\n    Row[\"SettingRow\\n(key, description, value)\"]\n    EditState[\"inline edit state\\n(useState per row)\"]\n    PutMutation[\"useMutation PUT /settings/key\"]\n    DelMutation[\"useMutation DELETE /settings/key\"]\n\n    SystemSettings --\u003e Query\n    SystemSettings --\u003e Groups\n    Groups --\u003e Accordion\n    Accordion --\u003e Row\n    Row --\u003e EditState\n    EditState --\u003e PutMutation\n    Row --\u003e DelMutation\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Setting Groups (categories)\n\nThe &#96;SETTING_GROUPS&#96; constant will define 12 categories. Each entry has &#96;key&#96;, &#96;label&#96;, &#96;description&#96;, &#96;isSecret&#96; flag, and optional &#96;defaultValue&#96; shown as placeholder:\n\n- **AI / Claude** — &#96;anthropic.api.key&#96; (secret), &#96;settings.encryption.key&#96; (secret), all &#96;webhook.secret.*&#96; keys (secret)\n- **Agent Behavior** — max-concurrent-jobs, blocked-paths, allowed-commands, max-files-changed, max-loop-iterations, job-timeout, self-review flags\n- **Schedulers** — quality-report, upgrade, and code-graph scheduler enabled/branch/timeout keys\n- **Linter / SAST** — all &#96;linter.*&#96; Good call — here's a smart breakdown of which input types would improve each setting, and how the implementation would work.

## Input type taxonomy

**Boolean toggle (immediate save on click, no edit form):**
All `*.enabled`, `*.self-review.enabled`, `planner.enabled`, `linter.fail-on-new-issues`, `linter.report-on-pr`, `linter.scope-to-changed-files`, `review.pr-summary.enabled`, `review.sequence-diagrams.enabled`, `code-graph.cross-repo.enabled`

The toggle shows the effective state: if overridden, use the stored value; if not overridden, use the `defaultValue` from the catalog but render it visually dimmed to indicate "using default". Clicking it immediately fires `PUT /settings/{key}` — no pencil/edit form needed.

**Select / dropdown:**

| Setting | Options |
|---|---|
| `git.platform` | `bitbucket`, `azuredevops`, `gitlab`, `github` |
| `anthropic.model` | `claude-opus-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022`, `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` |
| `anthropic.fast-model` | same list |
| `voyage.model` | `voyage-code-3`, `voyage-3`, `voyage-3-lite` |
| `jira.default.worklog` | `15m`, `30m`, `1h`, `2h` |

**Number input** (with `min` where sensible):
All timeout/minutes, max-*, token counts, pricing decimals, batch sizes, thresholds. Shows a `type="number"` input with appropriate `min`/`step`.

**Textarea** (values that contain commas/lists):
`run-fix.blocked-paths`, `run-fix.allowed-commands`, `tools.fetch-url.allowed-domains`, `quality-report.branches`, `review.webhook.skip-authors` — these are comma-separated lists that benefit from a wider, multi-line area.

**Password (already done):** all `isSecret: true` fields stay as-is.

**Text:** everything else.

   - Pencil + save form flow stays the same for non-boolean types

Clean. Here's a summary of what changed:

**New `SettingMeta` fields:**
- `inputType` — `'text' | 'boolean' | 'number' | 'select' | 'textarea'`
- `options` — dropdown choices for `select`
- `min` / `max` / `step` — constraints for `number`

**`BooleanSettingRow`** — completely replaces the pencil/edit-form pattern for boolean settings with an inline toggle pill. Shows a dimmed `"default"` label when not overridden. Clicking the toggle immediately fires `PUT` with the flipped value. Trash icon resets to default (only when overridden).

**`EditableSettingRow`** — the pencil → inline form flow, but the form element is now:
- `<select>` for `git.platform`, model pickers, `jira.default.worklog`, `voyage.model`
- `<input type="number">` with `min`/`max`/`step` for all numeric values (timeouts, token counts, thresholds, pricing)
- `<textarea rows={3}>` for comma-separated list fields (`blocked-paths`, `allowed-commands`, `skip-authors`, `allowed-domains`, etc.)
- Password input with show/hide for secrets (unchanged)
- Plain text input for everything else

**Smart defaults pre-filled** — when you open the edit form on an unset setting, the input is pre-populated with the `defaultValue` from the catalog so you can adjust from a sensible baseline rather than typing from scratch.
